Leadership · Business intelligence

Executive analytics dashboard

How real-time business intelligence dashboards gave a leadership team a single, current view of performance, replacing slow, manually assembled reports.

Let's Talk All case studies
Sector
Leadership
Focus areas
  • Business intelligence
  • Analytics
Related
Business intelligence · Custom software development
Client
Confidential
Overview

Good decisions depend on timely information. For this leadership team, the information existed, but it arrived late and from several directions at once, often after someone had spent time pulling it together. We built a set of real-time dashboards that bring the key measures of the business into one place, so leaders can see what is happening now, not what happened last month.

The challenge

What needed to change

Leadership lacked a timely, single view of business performance.

Performance information came from different systems and was compiled by hand into reports. By the time a report was ready it was already out of date, and comparing figures from different sources took further effort.

What was getting in the way

  • Information that arrived late

    Reports were assembled after the fact, so leaders were often looking at a picture that had already changed.

  • Several versions of the numbers

    Figures from different sources didn't always line up, which led to time spent reconciling instead of deciding.

  • Manual effort behind every report

    Producing a view of performance meant collecting and formatting data by hand each time.

  • Hard to spot change early

    Without a live view, emerging trends and issues could go unnoticed until the next reporting cycle.

The solution

What we delivered

We built real-time business intelligence dashboards that support faster strategic decisions.

The dashboards draw on the business's own data and present the measures leadership cares about most in one consistent view. Information refreshes as the business moves, so meetings start from current figures rather than a compiled report.

Key capabilities

  1. 01

    A single view of performance

    The key measures of the business brought together in one consistent set of dashboards.

  2. 02

    Real-time data

    Dashboards that reflect the current position rather than a point-in-time report.

  3. 03

    One definition of each measure

    Figures calculated the same way every time, so everyone discusses the same numbers.

  4. 04

    Drill-down from summary to detail

    Leaders can start with the headline and move into the detail behind it when they need to.

  5. 05

    No manual report-building

    The effort of collecting and formatting data for every report is removed.

Our approach

What shaped the solution

The priorities that guided the design and delivery.

  • Start from the decisions

    Each dashboard was built around the questions leadership needs to answer, not around the data that happened to be available.

  • Clarity over volume

    Fewer, well-chosen measures presented clearly, instead of every possible chart on one screen.

  • Trustworthy numbers

    Consistent definitions and connected data sources, so the dashboards can be relied on in important discussions.

The impact

What changed for the business

  • Decisions based on current information

    Leaders now work from a live view of performance instead of waiting for reports.

  • Less time compiling, more time acting

    The manual work of assembling reports no longer stands between the data and the decision.

  • Earlier sight of change

    Trends and issues become visible as they develop, not at the end of a reporting cycle.

How we work

How we approach projects like this

Every engagement follows the same clear path, adapted to the size and needs of the project.

  1. 01

    Discover

    Learn the goals, users, systems and constraints.

  2. 02

    Strategize

    Agree scope, priorities, roadmap and budget.

  6. 06
